proof_summary: Exhaustive primality-and-decomposition searches handle Goldbach for even \(4\le n\le8012\) and Lemoine for odd \(7\le n\le15727\); above those bounds, positivity supplies a witness \(q\), giving the required decompositions with \(p=n-q\) or \(p=n-2q\). For any bound \(N\), applying the hypothesis to \(n=2N+8014\) yields \(2q<n\), so \(r=n-q-6>N\) while both \(r\) and \(r+6=n-q\) are prime, proving the cousin-prime set is unbounded and hence infinite.
